title: Left Front Door Speakers: Removal and Installation
introduction:
This procedure covers the left front door midwoofer and woofer on vehicles with the documented MyFord Touch interface. The source heading covers SYNC 2/SYNC 3, but this complete workflow is limited to the supplied MyFord Touch operating instructions; verify that interface before work. Most of the work is getting the door trim out of the way: the speakers themselves have straightforward bolt mountings and electrical connectors. I treat the trim like a jacket with hidden buttons—find and release each attachment before trying to take it off.

The preparation below explains the linked trim-panel and window-switch access procedures. Their drawings show LHD, with RHD similar; the trim-panel drawings show the RH side, with LH similar. The switch-access drawing shows LH, with RH similar. This is a removal and installation guide; its ordinary completion checks do not diagnose a sound complaint.

requirements.category: Match the documented audio interface before starting

items.name: MyFord Touch interface required for this complete workflow
items.detail: Before dismantling anything, confirm that the fitted system has the documented MyFord Touch Home screen with the lower-left Entertainment corner, AM/FM tabs and the Power, VOL, TUNE and Seek controls described in the completion check. This workflow narrows the source’s SYNC 2/SYNC 3 heading to the interface supported by the supplied owner instructions. If the car has SYNC 3 or a different interface, stop before dismantling and obtain the complete matching owner control sequence and applicable repair instructions; this article does not verify that branch.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Park on level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked; keep P selected on an automatic or a parked gear on a manual. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling anything. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the car, causing personal injury or death. If the setting needs ignition power, keep the valid intelligent access key inside. From confirmed OFF, press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to select engine-off ON. If already ON for the settings, leave it ON rather than toggling it. After the setting change, return ON to OFF by pressing and releasing the button without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave it OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before service to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury. Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

items.name: Protect yourself while handling the panel
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection when servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling components with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to follow these precautions may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Have trim and torque tools ready
items.detail: The window-switch illustration shows a trim-removal tool for lifting the bezel assembly. Have suitable fastener tools and a torque wrench capable of the low tightening values given here. The supplied evidence does not identify fastener tool sizes.

items.name: Expose the upper trim attachment
items.detail: Remove the small cover inside the interior door-release handle recess, then remove the upper trim-panel bolt behind it. Its installation torque is 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm). See [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600).

items.name: Remove the window-switch and bezel assembly
items.detail: Lift the window-switch bezel assembly from the armrest, releasing its four retaining clips, then disconnect the switch electrical connector underneath. This access operation applies to both doors. Separating the switch itself from the bezel is only necessary when installing a new component; it is not needed simply to remove the assembly for speaker access. See [Front Door Window Control Switch](#/document/G1695936).

items.name: Remove the remaining threaded trim attachments
items.detail: After removing the switch assembly, remove the center trim-panel bolt exposed in the armrest opening. Its installation torque is 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm). Then remove the two lower retainers along the underside of the panel; their installation torque is 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm).

items.name: Release the rear upper edge
items.detail: At the latch-side upper edge, ease the trim away from the door. Release the upper clip first, then the two pin-type retainers farther down that rear edge. Work at the attachment locations rather than pulling the entire panel at once.

items.name: Release the rear and lower edge
items.detail: Continue around the lower edge. Release the pin-type retainer near the lower rear corner first, then release the clip near the lower front corner beside the large speaker grille. Move the freed rear and lower portions away from the door.

items.name: Release the front edge
items.detail: At the hinge-side edge, release the lower pin-type retainer first. Then release both pin-type retainers farther up that edge. The upper group contains two retainers, so releasing only one leaves the panel attached.

items.name: Free the panel from its remaining connections
items.detail: Lift the panel up and out to disengage it from the door. Disconnect the panel electrical connectors, if equipped. Working behind the interior handle, draw the highlighted latch-cable fitting out of its retaining seat beside the handle return spring, diagonally down and away in the rear-handle view, and disengage the cable from the handle. That movement describes the view from behind the panel, not a vehicle-forward direction. Once the cable and connectors are free, remove the panel. See [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600) for the rear-handle view.

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal steps before starting; they also contain details needed during installation.
edits.why: The tightening values sit beside the removal instructions, so keep them available for reassembly.

edits.text: Remove the front door trim panel to expose the speakers. Use the access sequence above and the linked [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600) procedure (501-05 Interior Trim and Ornamentation, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: The panel has concealed fasteners, perimeter retainers, electrical connections where equipped, and a latch cable. Releasing those attachments in sequence gives access without treating the wiring or cable as a carrying strap.
Use the illustration to identify the midwoofer assembly with the roughly rectangular mounting face.

edits.text: Remove the mounting bolts and ease the door midwoofer speaker out of its mounting position, keeping it supported while you disconnect its electrical connector.
edits.why: The illustration highlights three mounting bolts around the assembly. Supporting the released speaker keeps its weight off the attached wiring.

edits.text: Release and unplug the midwoofer electrical connector at the lower edge of the assembly. During installation, tighten the speaker mounting bolts to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm).
edits.why: The torque applies to the mounting bolts, not the electrical connector. With the plug disconnected, the speaker is free of the door wiring.
The woofer illustration shows the larger circular assembly and its perimeter mounting points.

edits.text: Remove the mounting bolts and ease the door woofer speaker out of its mounting position, keeping it supported while you disconnect its electrical connector.
edits.why: The illustration highlights three mounting bolts. Keep the released assembly supported until its wiring connection is free.

edits.text: Release and unplug the woofer electrical connector at the lower edge of the assembly. During installation, tighten the speaker mounting bolts to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm).
edits.why: This value secures the speaker mounting bolts; it is not a tightening instruction for the plug. Disconnecting the plug completes the speaker removal.

edits.text: Install by reversing the removal sequence. Reconnect each removed speaker's electrical connector, position the speaker in its mounting location, and install its bolts at the tightening value given beside that speaker's removal instructions. Transfer trim-panel parts as necessary. Re-engage the latch cable with the interior handle and return its fitting into the retaining seat beside the return spring, reversing the release movement described above. Reconnect the trim-panel electrical connectors, if equipped. Engage the panel's upper edge by reversing the up-and-out removal movement, then seat the perimeter attachments in reverse order: the upper hinge-side retainers, lower hinge-side retainer, lower front clip, lower rear retainer, rear-edge retainers, and rear upper clip. Reinstall the lower threaded retainers and center bolt at the preparation values. Reconnect the window-switch electrical connector and seat the switch-and-bezel assembly in its retaining clips. Finish by installing the upper trim-panel bolt at its preparation value and refitting the handle-recess cover.
edits.why:
Reconnecting the cable and wiring before seating the panel restores the connections that will become concealed. Reversing the attachment sequence brings the panel back onto its mounting points, with the cable fitting seated and the clips engaged.

After all wiring and trim are restored, keep the car parked in P for an automatic or a parked gear for a manual, with the parking brake applied, wheels chocked and the engine stopped. With the valid key inside, start from ignition OFF and press the start button without pressing either pedal to switch the ignition ON without starting the engine. For the documented MyFord Touch interface, if the audio is OFF, press the audio Power button to turn it ON; if it has already resumed ON, leave it ON rather than toggling it. Touch the Home icon, then the lower-left Entertainment corner and the AM or FM tab. Turn TUNE or press Seek to find a familiar station, then turn VOL to a comfortable level and listen for sound from the serviced door speakers. This is an ordinary function check, not fault isolation. After listening, press the audio Power control to turn the audio OFF. With ignition still in the known engine-off ON state, check the disturbed window switch: keep children and pets away and hands and objects clear of the glass; press the window switch to open the window and lift it to close. Confirm normal response without testing or overriding bounce-back. Press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to return the known ON state to OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key. Keep the parked gear, parking brake and wheel restraints in place. Gently open and close the door with its handle, confirming the interior handle releases the latch and the door latches normally without forcing it. These are ordinary checks of the disturbed controls and connections, not electrical diagnosis or door alignment. If sound, window response, handle action or retention is abnormal, stop before driving and keep ignition OFF/key out before reopening trim or checking a connector. See the [matching owner manual, Audio, Windows and Starting](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/Catalog/owner_information/2015-Mustang-Owners-Manual-version-1_om_EN-US_07_2014.pdf) for the fitted controls.

editorialRevision.scope: Keep primary speaker action text and torques unchanged; provide exact matched audio interface before work, known parked ignition setup and owner-backed audio/window/ordinary handle completion. For SYNC remove unrelated switch replacement branch and clarify both upper hinge retainers and separate cable attachments; complete prior source/figure review retained, independent increment recorded separately.
